content: The study evaluates the effects of various tocolytic agents on delaying preterm birth and their associated neonatal outcomes. The interventions analyzed include beta-mimetics, calcium channel blockers, COX inhibitors, magnesium sulfate, nitric oxide donors, oxytocin receptor antagonists, and combinations of tocolytics. These were compared against placebo or no treatment in hospital settings. Neonatal Death Before 7 Days The analysis indicates that nitric oxide donors and combinations of tocolytics were not estimable for their effects on neonatal death within the first 7 days of life. Direct evidence for some interventions was downgraded due to multiple limitations in study design and serious imprecision. Neonatal Death Before 28 Days The study assessed the impact of tocolytics on neonatal death within 28 days of birth. Evidence quality varied, with some interventions showing very low certainty due to serious imprecision and study design limitations. Ranking of tocolytics was based on cumulative probabilities of being the most effective agent, with larger SUCRA (Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking) values indicating higher ranks. Respiratory Morbidity The effects of tocolytics on respiratory morbidity in neonates were analyzed. Evidence quality was often very low, with significant limitations in study design and imprecision. Rankings were determined using cumulative probabilities, with SUCRA values used to assess the relative effectiveness of each agent. Neurodevelopmental Morbidity The study examined the impact of tocolytics on neurodevelopmental outcomes in neonates. Evidence quality was frequently downgraded due to very low certainty, stemming from study design limitations and imprecision. Rankings were again based on cumulative probabilities, with SUCRA values indicating the relative effectiveness of each intervention. Gastrointestinal Morbidity The analysis included the effects of tocolytics on gastrointestinal morbidity in neonates. Evidence quality was very low, with significant limitations and imprecision noted in the studies. Rankings were determined using cumulative probabilities, with SUCRA values indicating the relative effectiveness of each agent. Mean Birth Weight The study evaluated the impact of tocolytics on mean birth weight. Evidence quality was downgraded due to multiple limitations in study design and serious imprecision. Rankings were based on cumulative probabilities, with SUCRA values used to assess the relative effectiveness of each intervention. Evidence Grading Evidence was frequently downgraded due to limitations in study design, serious or very serious imprecision, and inconsistencies in the data. Direct, indirect, and network evidence were all subject to downgrading based on these factors. The color coding in the network diagrams (green for high certainty, light green for moderate certainty, orange for low certainty, and red for very low certainty) visually represented the quality of evidence. Conclusion The study provides a comprehensive network meta-analysis of tocolytic agents for delaying preterm birth and their effects on neonatal outcomes. The findings highlight the variability in evidence quality and the need for further high-quality research to establish the most effective interventions.
